## 中建二局承建的腾讯广州总部大楼项目通过竣工验收

发布日期：2025-08-07
    〖字体：大中小〗打印

　　近日，由中建二局承建的腾讯广州总部大楼项目顺利通过竣工验收。

Image: 〖局报第25期+2版+图片新闻〗华南公司+华南公司腾讯广州总部大楼项目顺利通过竣工验收 (2).jpg

　　项目位于广州市琶洲互联网创新集聚区核心区，总建筑面积17.4万平方米，建筑高度206.75米，是集科研、办公及配套设施综合为一体的超高层建筑。项目建成后将成为广州核心区代表性建筑之一，与珠江西城、广州国际金融城隔江相望，构成广州中心城区的“黄金三角洲”，共同助推粤港澳大湾区腾飞。（中建二局供稿）

# 

腾讯广州总部大楼开始交付

## 

Image

    近日，由中建二局承建的腾讯广州总部大楼项目落成并开始交付。这座高达206.75米的新地标由法国建筑师让·努维尔设计，设计理念以“生活、交流、开放”为核心，将成为腾讯的微信总部。

    项目技术负责人介绍，该建筑采用“垂直城市”理念，设置4道单边悬挑平台，分别从14、23、32、38层向外伸出，打造出花园、山丘、村庄、屋顶等不同主题的“空中聚落”，融入丰富自然生态，打破传统办公楼的冰冷感。其中，38层悬挑跨度达28米，重达750吨，面积相当于4个标准篮球场，属国内首例最大高空大悬挑平台结构。

    南方日报记者 邵一弘

　　今年7月，广州市海珠区住房和建设局官网发布公告，宣布腾讯广州总部大楼已顺利通过竣工联合验收开启运营，连同琶洲各大互联网巨头一起，与珠江新城、广州国际金融城隔江相望，构成广州中心城区的“黄金三角洲”。资料显示，腾讯广州总部大楼自 2017 年项目设计启动，大楼高达 207 米，共 39 层，总建筑面积17.4万平方米。该建筑采用“垂直城市”理念，设置4道单边悬挑平台，创下国内超高层直挑结构首例。该建筑包含智慧办公、公共艺术空间及市民开放区域，为腾讯在粤港澳大湾区的重要战略布局，将可容纳5000余名员工办公。据南方+记者了解到，该大楼的设计师是法国当代著名建筑师让・努维尔，曾获得了普利兹克奖、阿卡汗奖、沃尔夫艺术奖等权威大奖。他参与设计的建筑作品横跨五大洲，多达200余个，包括浦东美术馆、深圳歌剧院。

# 让·努维尔新作：腾讯广州大厦，珠江之畔“垂直城市”

让·努维尔新作：腾讯广州大厦，珠江之畔“垂直城市”

编辑：王子萱 | 校对：王子萱 | 2026.05.29 18:14

Image项目外观  ©有方

设计单位  Ateliers Jean Nouvel

项目地点  广东广州

建成时间  2025年

建筑面积  约180,000平方米

* * *

 

本文文字由Ateliers Jean Nouvel提供。

 

在广州琶洲的珠江岸线，一座38层、高206.75米的垂直地标，正重新定义超高层总部建筑。由普利兹克奖得主让·努维尔领衔设计的腾讯广州大厦，以“生活、交流、向世界开放”为核心理念，在塑造腾讯现代而庄重的企业形象的同时，自豪地展现了其所创造的工作环境。

 

在这座建筑面积约170,421平方米、以办公功能为主的超高层建筑中，裙楼作为24小时开放的公共空间，向公众全面开放；而在间隔约每十层的平台层上，小体量的建筑单元将休闲与办公功能充分融合其中，创造出一种独特的办公建筑类型。

# 腾讯广州总部大楼搬迁启用，门口布置成“登机口”

2025-09-09 22:07 来源:大洋网

腾讯广州总部大楼正式搬迁启用。9月9日，记者在大楼的入口处看到，已有不少腾讯员工以及相关人员进进出出。大楼门口的电梯处布置成一个机场“登机口”的造型，大拱门上写着“乔迁大吉”，目的地“腾讯广州大厦”，航班号“TG0908”。

记者从相关人士处了解到，目前有部分员工搬进腾讯广州总部大楼，但是还没有全面进驻。9月8日，有网友就晒出了当天乔迁仪式现场，不仅有舞狮表演，更有丰富精美的茶点、礼物等，非常热闹。现场摆放的背景板上写着“珠江潮起，腾跃星辰”。

据了解，腾讯广州总部大楼位于海珠区芳园路99号，定位为“微信生态中枢”，主要业务围绕微信展开。该建筑采用“垂直城市”理念，设置4道单边悬挑平台，创下国内超高层直挑结构首例。建筑内包含智慧办公、公共艺术空间及市民开放区域，是腾讯在粤港澳大湾区的重要战略布局，将可容纳5000余名员工办公。

What Went into Designing the Headquarters of Tencent, Asia's Most Valuable Company (https://www.architecturaldigest.com/story/designing-headquarters-tencent-asias-most-valuable-company)
【turn7news25】 [wordlim: 100] Published: 10.1 years ago; Tencent commissioned New York architecture firm NBBJ to design its $599 million headquarters in Shenzhen, scheduled for completion in 2017. The headquarters reflects Tencent’s innovation-driven culture and aims to strengthen community, employee well-being, and collaboration. Its two towers are connected by multistory skybridges that intersect at different levels and contain shared spaces organized around themes such as health, culture, and education. Rather than serving merely as visual features, the bridges are intended to encourage spontaneous interactions among teams and reduce the isolation often associated with high-rise offices. The building will also incorporate Tencent technology, including hologram-guided tours to help visitors and employees navigate the complex. Environmental strategies include orienting the building to use prevailing winds for natural ventilation, minimizing solar exposure, employing self-shading curtain walls, and using solar and energy modeling. Computational design will optimize shading between the towers. Together, these measures are expected to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions by 40 percent compared with a typical office tower. The project’s central challenge was redefining the corporate skyscraper as a healthier, more connected workplace.
What Went into Designing the Headquarters of Tencent, Asia’s Most Valuable Company
Date: Tue Sep 20 23:05:36 2016 UTC

Fortune 500 companies spend billions to ensure the proper image of their brand-which is why they often spare no expense when it comes to building their headquarters. And it's in China, where many newcomers to the Fortune 500 list can be found, that some of the most innovative new offices are located. Near the top of the Fortune 500 list is Tencent, an investment holdings firm that specializes in internet services. Valued at $246 billion, Tencent is Asia's most profitable company. In 2013, the firm enlisted New York-based architecture group NBBJ to build its new $599 million headquarters in Shenzhen. Scheduled for completion in 2017, the building is connected by a series of skybridges and features such state-of-the-art technology as hologram-led tours of the space. Architectural Digest talked to NBBJ design partner Jonathan Ward about the design of Tencent's new headquarters.
Architectural Digest: In what way did the day-to-day culture at Tencent factor into the design of the new HQ?
Jonathan Ward: Tencent's corporate culture is focused on creating innovative products and experiences that help its customers better communicate, shop, socialize, and play. Therefore it was paramount that its cultural emphasis on innovation be echoed and reinforced in the design of its new headquarters. The design draws employees together more frequently and in new ways. The multistory connecting bridges, for example, which intersect at various floors, aren't just visual aesthetics, but they also house most of the common areas for employees to interact.
AD: In New York, SHoP Architects has been constructing a skyscraper that features two buildings and a skybridge meant to suggest a dancing couple. Did any similar themes go into the decision to create multiple skybridges in your skyscraper?
JW: We certainly did not have the theme of a dancing couple in mind when designing the project. The Tencent project is the result of a multiyear design process. The primary drivers for the project were to heighten the sense of community among its employees, increase social well-being, and encourage serendipitous interactions between teams. The critical solution for these desires are the bridge links, which incorporate specific themes such as health, culture and education to help its employees think and work differently than they had before.
AD: Is it true that guests will be ushered through the building through hologram tours?
JW: Yes, that is true. The hologram tours are the result of an initiative to integrate Tencent's own technology into its headquarters. The technology will help employees and guests more easily navigate the building and take advantage of its many amenities. Since it's a big advancement in design technology, Tencent is still not ready to release more details about the program.
AD: What are some of the eco-friendly measures you took with this building?
JW: We rotated the original design to take advantage of the site's prevailing winds to ventilate the atria, while minimizing exposure to direct sun. To control glare and heat gain, the curtain wall incorporates a modular self-shading system that varies based on the degree of sun exposure. Solar and energy modeling were utilized to minimize solar heat gain during intense sun periods. Also, we used a computational design to optimize the amount that the south tower shades the north tower. These and other energy strategies will reduce consumption and carbon emissions by 40 percent over a typical office tower.
AD: What was the most difficult element in designing the HQ?
JW: The Tencent headquarters is located on a tight urban site, which always presents challenges. But perhaps the greatest challenge is one we brought upon ourselves: We sought to use this project to rethink and redefine the corporate high-rise. While great at accommodating lots of people in one place, tall buildings are also notorious for creating barriers between people, teams and departments. As more companies and especially those in the tech industry move into the city, we wanted to create a high-rise design for Tencent that would promote connection, innovation, and health. Using the bridge links, offset cores, a transparent interior design, and advanced elevator systems, the design will help to overcome these barriers.

Building Instance Classification Using Street View Images (https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.09026)
【turn7academia32】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 8.7 years ago; 
Title: Building Instance Classification Using Street View Images
Authors: Jian Kang, Marco Körner, Yuanyuan Wang, Hannes Taubenböck, Xiao Xiang Zhu
Date: Sun Feb 25 16:04:34 2018

Land-use classification based on spaceborne or aerial remote sensing images has been extensively studied over the past decades. Such classification is usually a patch-wise or pixel-wise labeling over the whole image. But for many applications, such as urban population density mapping or urban utility planning, a classification map based on individual buildings is much more informative. However, such semantic classification still poses some fundamental challenges, for example, how to retrieve fine boundaries of individual buildings. In this paper, we proposed a general framework for classifying the functionality of individual buildings. The proposed method is based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) which classify facade structures from street view images, such as Google StreetView, in addition to remote sensing images which usually only show roof structures. Geographic information was utilized to mask out individual buildings, and to associate the corresponding street view images. We created a benchmark dataset which was used for training and evaluating CNNs. In addition, the method was applied to generate building classification maps on both region and city scales of several cities in Canada and the US. Keywords: CNN, Building instance classification, Street view images, OpenStreetMap

Rethinking Bottleneck Structure for Efficient Mobile Network Design (https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.02269)
【turn7academia33】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 6.3 years ago; 
Title: Rethinking Bottleneck Structure for Efficient Mobile Network Design
Authors: Zhou Daquan, Qibin Hou, Yunpeng Chen, Jiashi Feng, Shuicheng Yan
Date: Sun Jul  5 08:55:26 2020

The inverted residual block is dominating architecture design for mobile networks recently. It changes the classic residual bottleneck by introducing two design rules: learning inverted residuals and using linear bottlenecks. In this paper, we rethink the necessity of such design changes and find it may bring risks of information loss and gradient confusion. We thus propose to flip the structure and present a novel bottleneck design, called the sandglass block, that performs identity mapping and spatial transformation at higher dimensions and thus alleviates information loss and gradient confusion effectively. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, different from the common belief, such bottleneck structure is more beneficial than the inverted ones for mobile networks. In ImageNet classification, by simply replacing the inverted residual block with our sandglass block without increasing parameters and computation, the classification accuracy can be improved by more than 1.7% over MobileNetV2. On Pascal VOC 2007 test set, we observe that there is also 0.9% mAP improvement in object detection. We further verify the effectiveness of the sandglass block by adding it into the search space of neural architecture search method DARTS. With 25% parameter reduction, the classification accuracy is improved by 0.13% over previous DARTS models. Code can be found at: https://github.com/zhoudaquan/rethinking_bottleneck_design.

Building Facade Parsing R-CNN (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05912)
【turn7academia34】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 4.5 years ago; 
Title: Building Facade Parsing R-CNN
Authors: Sijie Wang, Qiyu Kang, Rui She, Wee Peng Tay, Diego Navarro Navarro, Andreas Hartmannsgruber
Date: Thu May 12 07:08:45 2022

Building facade parsing, which predicts pixel-level labels for building facades, has applications in computer vision perception for autonomous vehicle (AV) driving. However, instead of a frontal view, an on-board camera of an AV captures a deformed view of the facade of the buildings on both sides of the road the AV is travelling on, due to the camera perspective. We propose Facade R-CNN, which includes a transconv module, generalized bounding box detection, and convex regularization, to perform parsing of deformed facade views. Experiments demonstrate that Facade R-CNN achieves better performance than the current state-of-the-art facade parsing models, which are primarily developed for frontal views. We also publish a new building facade parsing dataset derived from the Oxford RobotCar dataset, which we call the Oxford RobotCar Facade dataset. This dataset contains 500 street-view images from the Oxford RobotCar dataset augmented with accurate annotations of building facade objects. The published dataset is available at https://github.com/sijieaaa/Oxford-RobotCar-Facade

Understanding Mobile Traffic Patterns of Large Scale Cellular Towers in Urban Environment (https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.04026)
【turn7academia35】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 11.0 years ago; 
Title: Understanding Mobile Traffic Patterns of Large Scale Cellular Towers in Urban Environment
Authors: Huandong Wang, Fengli Xu, Yong Li, Pengyu Zhang, Depeng Jin
Date: Wed Oct 14 10:01:07 2015

Understanding mobile traffic patterns of large scale cellular towers in urban environment is extremely valuable for Internet service providers, mobile users, and government managers of modern metropolis. This paper aims at extracting and modeling the traffic patterns of large scale towers deployed in a metropolitan city. To achieve this goal, we need to address several challenges, including lack of appropriate tools for processing large scale traffic measurement data, unknown traffic patterns, as well as handling complicated factors of urban ecology and human behaviors that affect traffic patterns. Our core contribution is a powerful model which combines three dimensional information (time, locations of towers, and traffic frequency spectrum) to extract and model the traffic patterns of thousands of cellular towers. Our empirical analysis reveals the following important observations. First, only five basic time-domain traffic patterns exist among the 9,600 cellular towers. Second, each of the extracted traffic pattern maps to one type of geographical locations related to urban ecology, including residential area, business district, transport, entertainment, and comprehensive area. Third, our frequency-domain traffic spectrum analysis suggests that the traffic of any tower among the 9,600 can be constructed using a linear combination of four primary components corresponding to human activity behaviors. We believe that the proposed traffic patterns extraction and modeling methodology, combined with the empirical analysis on the mobile traffic, pave the way toward a deep understanding of the traffic patterns of large scale cellular towers in modern metropolis.

L139: 在广州琶洲的珠江岸线，一座38层、高206.75米的垂直地标，正重新定义超高层总部建筑。由普利兹克奖得主让·努维尔领衔设计的腾讯广州大厦，以“生活、交流、向世界开放”为核心理念，在塑造腾讯现代而庄重的企业形象的同时，自豪地展现了其所创造的工作环境。
L140: 
L141: 
L142: 
L143: 在这座建筑面积约170,421平方米、以办公功能为主的超高层建筑中，裙楼作为24小时开放的公共空间，向公众全面开放；而在间隔约每十层的平台层上，小体量的建筑单元将休闲与办公功能充分融合其中，创造出一种独特的办公建筑类型。
L144: 建筑师以八大核心元素为基石，将建筑与城市、珠江、自然、生态、光线、色彩深度融合，实践着垂直城市中的人文主义。

L149: # 01 城市性：向公众敞开的城市客厅
L150: 
L151: 腾讯大厦是友好而热情的城市界面。南侧激活城市广场，面向公众开放的步行流线从南广场出发，穿越地块景观通廊直抵江边，构筑起一条欣赏广州天际线的公共通道。局部镂空的平台交叠布置，在打造立体花园系统的同时，也为地上和地下空间引入充足的自然光线。建筑不再是封闭的企业容器，而是融入城市肌理、服务市民的开放公共空间。

L162: # 02 滨江性：拥抱珠江的空中景观平台
L163: 
L164: 建筑沿珠江打造大型观景平台，为休闲与娱乐活动提供空中露台。面向城市与珠江的视线走廊被精心预留，建筑立面在江面形成灵动的倒影；微微倾斜的外立面捕捉河流波光，映照江上生活与往来船只，让建筑成为珠江景观的有机组成部分。

L190: # 04 创造性：融合工作与生活的新类型学
L191: 
L192: 大厦创造了融合生活乐趣与工作效率的建筑新范式。约每十层设置一处“空中花园”，布置瑜伽室、图书馆、餐厅及会议室等多元功能空间。不同尺度的空间对比激活了场所的独特性，让垂直办公拥有了水平社区的温度与活力。让员工在高强度工作中，也能感受到社区般的舒适与归属感。除了这些“空中花园”，办公层还拥有各自的室外露台，所有这些室外空间通过旋转楼梯串联，形成一个可漫游的垂直的绿化空间。

L210: # 05 生态：舒适节能的快乐建筑
L211: 
L212: 通过花园系统与不同朝向立面的优化，建筑形成了一套综合环境策略。倾斜的高反射立面有效降低太阳直射带来的影响，北立面与阴影区域则采用高透光玻璃，以提升自然采光，在控制能耗的同时，营造稳定而舒适的室内微气候。内立面上特殊的建筑开口形式，将南侧日照引入建筑内部及“空中花园”，同时更好地适应广州当地气候条件，发挥良好的自然通风效果。

L226: # 07 鲜活感：色彩变幻的情感办公世界
L227: 
L228: 大厦被构想为一个充满情感与惊喜的“办公世界”。多元色彩与材料交织，塑造出步移景异的独特体验；光线穿过建筑内侧的分色玻璃，形成衍射后的光线辐射效应，强化了明暗对比。夜晚，当内部灯光亮起时，彩色光影散落于外部空间。随着时间变化的彩色灯光、露台底板投影、植物景观以及吊顶上的镜像，与腾讯的创意活动形成动态互动，共同营造充满活力与想象力的办公氛围。

L243: # 08 人文主义：垂直城市的全新宣言
L244: 
L245: 腾讯广州大厦是人文主义在垂直城市中的实践宣言，创造出世界独一无二的办公建筑类型学。它超越功能容器的定义，成为承载生活、交流与开放精神的垂直社区，在珠江之滨书写科技企业与城市共生的新范式。

L264: 这座垂直城市，不仅是腾讯业务的新载体，更以开放姿态融入城市，成为琶洲互联网创新集聚区的精神坐标。它证明，超高层建筑可以在追求效率的同时，保留自然温度与人文关怀，让垂直空间成为连接城市、自然与人的纽带。
